Discover what you could build

TilePark XY

What would you build if parking didn’t dictate the design?

TilePark changes the architecture of parking itself. Independent conveyors move vehicles in every horizontal direction, while stackers handle vertical movement. No ramps, no drive aisles, no central transport bottlenecks. Just more cars in less space, with unprecedented architectural flexibility and a decentralized design engineered for reliability. Before you design or finance around parking, discover what you could build without its limitations.

The building that could have existed

Your building needs parking. It doesn’t need parking’s limitations.

For those who plan, build and fund buildings

A different architecture changes the economics of your building.

Every space in a conventional garage comes with its share of ramps and drive aisles. TilePark has neither. The floor you no longer give to cars can go back to the building: more apartments, more rentable space, less excavation. For owners, banks and investors, that means more income from the same site and less capital tied up in parking.

With TilePark, sites that never added up suddenly do.

Many projects fail on parking alone: the plot is too small, too irregular or too costly to excavate for ramps and drive aisles. TilePark needs far less floor area per car and follows the shape of the site. The space it unlocks becomes additional rentable units, the extra revenue carries the project, and sites that never added up become feasible.

Increase your IRR by unlocking valuable space.

How the architectures compare

Aisles cost space. TilePark has none.

AGV systems, rail-guided shuttles and moving tower systems all need at least one drive aisle, rails or central lifts. TilePark needs none: its patented XY technology turns the entire floor into parking.

At least 20 % more parking spaces on the same footprint than aisle-based automated parking systems.

AGV systemsRail-guided shuttlesMoving tower systemsTilePark XY
Drive aisles or railsYesYesYesNone
If one machine stopsA stalled robot can block the aisle it sharesA shuttle or lift fault blocks its aisle or levelA lift fault blocks the cars it servesCars route around an offline conveyor
Layout flexibilityFixed by the aisleFixed by railsFixed by the towerFits any plot, column grid and shape

Every automated garage shares infrastructure such as power supply and the control network, TilePark included. The difference is in the machines that move the cars: on the TilePark grid, an offline conveyor is routed around and the rest of the garage keeps working.

An infrastructure decision

A garage is built once. You live with it for decades.

Once ramps, drive aisles and lift shafts are cast in concrete, the parking decision shapes the building for its entire life. The real question is not whether TilePark is better today. It is what the alternatives will cost you over the next 30 years: in floor area, in flexibility, in asset value and in risk.

Questions to ask before you commit

Conventional garage

  • Ramps and drive aisles take a large share of every level, for the life of the building.
  • More excavation, or more levels, for the same number of cars.
  • Sloped ramps and low ceilings make later conversion difficult and costly.

Other automated parking systems

  • Does every car pass through a few central lifts or shuttles? Then they set your throughput.
  • How much can the system change once it is built?

TilePark XY

  • No ramps, no drive aisles: more than 150 sq ft per car goes back to the building.
  • Hundreds of independent conveyors and no central bottleneck. If one is offline, the others route around it.
  • A modular grid that fits irregular sites, and a decentralized architecture that keeps getting better through software, for decades.

Before you commit your building to a conventional layout or another automated parking system, find out what TilePark could change.

Inspired by nature · Distributed intelligence

Nature doesn’t need a central bottleneck. Neither should parking.

Bees coordinate thousands of movements without a central path, and simply work around a damaged cell. TilePark follows the same principle: independent conveyors, each with its own controller, and no central bottleneck.

The bees' rules for parking

  1. 1

    “Don't waste a single cell.”

    TileParkEvery position is a conveyor: no ramps, no drive aisles, no wasted floor.

  2. 2

    “Take the shortest way.”

    TileParkEvery request gets the fastest route for the grid’s current layout.

The heart of TilePark

No central control.
No central bottleneck.

Just like bees in a hive, each TilePark conveyor has its own controller and acts independently. There is no master computer, shuttle, or lift that every car depends on. This decentralized control is the core of our technology and the source of the system's speed, flexibility, and resilience.

Conveyors move in parallelMany conveyors move simultaneously, so no car has to wait for the one ahead of it.
A new route every timeEach sequence is calculated for the grid's current layout, so the system adapts rather than replaying a fixed program.
Robust by designA modular structure built from industry-standard components means fewer faults and fast replacement. Remote diagnostics let our team respond to any issue immediately.
A conveyor fault doesn’t stop the garageIf a conveyor goes offline, the others route around it, just like bees in a hive. Try "Simulate conveyor fault" in the sliding-puzzle demo above.

And if the power goes out? Your car still comes out.

TilePark requires remarkably little power. With as little as 30 amps, the entire system can run on a generator, so drivers can still collect their cars during a power outage.

  • Low energy use. On the XY level, cars only ever move horizontally, along the shortest optimized routes. Only the transport level is automated, and only the conveyors needed for a sequence move.
  • Built-in redundancy. Every conveyor has at least four drive motors, and if one conveyor is offline, the cars are routed around it.

Patented principle

The TilePark XY sliding-puzzle principle is protected by European patent EP 3924576 B1, with further patents pending in the US and Germany.

TilePark · The sliding puzzle

A garage that works like a sliding puzzle.

In a conventional garage, roughly half of the floor area is taken up by ramps and drive aisles. TilePark needs neither. Each car rests on a pallet, and the conveyors beneath move it lengthwise and sideways, just like the pieces of a sliding puzzle. A single empty space is enough to bring any car to the transfer cabin.

Flagship simulationAny car reaches the cabin, with no drive aisle, even with a conveyor offline.

TilePark Automated Stackers · The third dimension

Add Z. Up to four cars on the footprint of one.

The XY grid moves cars across the floor. Add a TilePark stacker above selected conveyors, or above every conveyor, and the footprint of a single car holds up to four cars instead of one, still without ramps, drive aisles, or a central lift tower.

XY handles the logistics

The transport level brings each car beneath its stacker, using the same sliding-puzzle routing.

The stacker lifts it up

The stacker raises the car into a storage level directly above its conveyor. The storage levels need no conveyors, because cars are stacked as in a silo.

And brings it back down

On request, the stacker lowers the car onto a free conveyor, which carries it to the transfer cabin.

Still no central bottleneck

Each stacker serves only its own conveyor. With no central lift tower that every car depends on, the rest of the garage keeps running.

Why Z pays off

One automation level. Everything above is simple storage.

All of the automation is concentrated on the ground floor; only the transport level has conveyors. The levels above are stacked like a silo and need neither conveyors nor floor slabs. The building becomes simpler, lower, and less expensive, and its full height can be used for parking.

Conveyors on one level onlyConveyors and drives are installed on the transport level alone. The storage levels are simple steel shelving, which means less equipment to purchase and maintain.
No slabs to buildA stacked silo replaces intermediate parking decks, eliminating the cost of concrete slabs, formwork, and reinforcement.
No height lost to slabsWithout slabs and their build-up, every meter of height is used for cars, so more levels fit within the same building.
Lower build-up heightThe XY conveyor level itself is very low, which saves floor height, pit depth and construction cost.
Lightweight constructionThe light steel structure means lower loads on the building, smaller foundations, and an easy fit in existing structures.
Less excavationA lower structure for the same number of cars means a shallower pit, reducing the cost of excavation, shoring, and waterproofing.

It unlocks height. Whether in a basement, on a ground floor, or in a dedicated building, the clear height you already have becomes parking capacity.

TilePark products

TilePark Tower

Built upwards.

Made for land in good locations that is hard to use for anything else: leftover plots, corners of existing parking lots, sites too small or too awkward for housing or retail. The TilePark Tower turns them into parking, charging and mobility hubs on the footprint of a small building.

Size
From 2 to 24 cars per level, up to 13 levels.
Parking levels
A steel rack around a central shaft, with up to 4 rows and 13 levels.
Vertical movement
The central lift moves the cars up and down and delivers them to the different levels, where TilePark conveyors receive the pallets and move them in X and Y.

How the Tower works

Drive in. The tower does the rest.

  1. 1

    Drive in

    Drive into the bright transfer cabin at ground level and step out. Check in at the terminal or in the app.

  2. 2

    Up the central lift

    The central lift carries the car on its pallet up the shaft to a free level.

  3. 3

    Into its space

    TilePark conveyors on that level receive the pallet and move it in X and Y to its space. Retrieval runs the same way in reverse.

Where the Tower fits

One tower, many uses.

Unused land and existing parking lots

Leftover plots and corners of surface parking lots in good locations become high-capacity parking on a small footprint, while the rest of the site stays free for other uses.

Presentation tower

A glass tower for dealers and brands: cars on display around the clock, visible from the street, and delivered to the customer at the push of a button.

Built into the building

The tower doesn’t have to stand alone: it can be built into a new building as its showroom, its façade or its parking core.

Urban EV charging station

Every pallet can charge. The tower moves charged cars away from the chargers, so a compact city site serves many electric vehicles.

Hub for autonomous taxis

A fully automated home for autonomous fleets: vehicles drive in, recharge or wait, and are ready on request, with nobody needed on site.

Park and ride at transit stops

Next to tram, train or bus stops: many cars on a small footprint and a short walk to public transport.

Car sharing and rental hubs

Pick-up and return points in the city centre, with check-in through the app and charging included.

Hotels, hospitals and offices

Parking for guests, patients or staff on plots where a conventional garage does not fit, run as a valet service through the app.

Parking for existing neighbourhoods

Adds the parking an existing neighbourhood lacks, on a single small plot and without digging a basement.

Tower experience

More than 25 years of car towers.

Since 1999, the Nussbaum engineering team has built automated car towers for car brands, dealers and an online car retailer in Europe and the USA. TilePark Tower builds on this experience and adds TilePark conveyors on every level, so cars move in X and Y and each level holds up to 24 cars.

Integrated EV charging

Every space can charge. Every charger keeps working.

With fixed charging bays, a fully charged car blocks the charger until its driver returns. TilePark moves each EV to a charger, charges it to the level requested in the app, and then moves it away so the next vehicle can charge. Chargers stay in use all night, and far fewer are needed. You can't control what you don't design and build yourself.

This conviction is part of our DNA. Our engineers design every TilePark system, our team writes the controls that run it, and our own factories in Kehl, Germany, and Gastonia, USA, build it from raw steel to finished conveyor, in 130,000 sq ft of production space. No importer, no third-party system, and no outside assembler stand between you and the people who built your garage.

Designed in-houseMechanical, electrical, and structural engineering by our own team, so every component is designed specifically for TilePark.
Our own controlsThe decentralized control system that runs every conveyor is developed in-house. We know every line of code.
Made in our own factoriesLaser cutting, bending, robotic welding, and assembly under our own roof, in Germany and the USA.
Spare parts for at least 30 yearsBecause we own the drawings, the tooling, and the production, we can supply spare parts for at least 30 years, independent of any supplier's catalog.
Every component serializedEach component carries a serial number and can be traced at any time, so we keep full control of quality and of our supply chain.
Industry-standard componentsProven industrial parts inside our own design: robust, widely available and easy to service.
Quality control

Every conveyor segment is tested under load.

Before a conveyor leaves our factory, it goes onto the test rig. A hydraulic press applies load from above while the drives run, just as they will under a parked car. Only conveyors that pass are released for shipping.

  • Drives, gearboxes and rollers run under load, not just switched on.
  • Structure and alignment are checked while the conveyor carries weight.
  • Every result is logged against the component's serial number.

From first sketch to decades of operation

99.5 %availability: the bar we build to

Below 99.5 % availability, a system has failed in the eyes of its users.

To hold TilePark to it, every phase stays in our hands: from the first sketch to decades of service. For owners and lenders, that means one accountable partner for the life of the asset.

  1. 1

    Planning

    Together with architects and developers from the first sketch: the grid, stackers, transfer cabins and EV charging fitted to the site and the building.

  2. 2

    Engineering

    Our engineers design the mechanical, electrical and structural system and configure the controls for your project.

  3. 3

    Manufacturing

    Built and pre-assembled in our own factories in Kehl and Gastonia. Every conveyor is load-tested before shipping.

  4. 4

    Commissioning

    Installed and commissioned by our own team, and handed over by the people who built it.

  5. 5

    After-sales service

    24/7 availability, remote diagnostics and updates, and spare parts for at least 30 years.

  • 24/7

    Our after-sales team is available around the clock, every day of the year.

  • Kiosk or app

    Drivers and operators reach us directly from the kiosk or the app, in their own language.

  • 99 % solved remotely

    Our after-sales team solves 99 % of all issues remotely, through remote diagnostics.

  • On site

    If an issue cannot be solved remotely, a Parkstory technician comes on site.

From our own ideas to industrial excellence

We design what we build, and we build what we have developed ourselves.

We believe that to truly master a technology, you must understand how to develop it, how to build it, and how to make it better. This conviction has shaped generations of engineering and manufacturing within the Nussbaum family and remains a defining principle of Parkstory today.

Innovation does not end with a design or a prototype. Only by mastering development and manufacturing together can we reach the precision, consistency and reliability we expect from our products.

MaterialsWhat each part is made of, and why.
Production methodsHow every part is made, and how to make it better.
TolerancesPrecision that holds from the first unit to the last.
Quality controlBuilt into the process, not added at the end.
One systemMechanics, electronics, controls and software together.

Quality is not something we inspect into a finished product. It is something we engineer into the product and the processes that create it.

Our commitment to engineering ownership, industrial competence and quality.

We develop the technology, master the processes, and take responsibility for the result.

Where we come from

Three traditions. One company.

Parkstory brings together three distinct traditions: more than 75 years of industrial engineering and manufacturing expertise rooted in the Nussbaum family, over 30 years of software development and digital innovation pioneered by Marc Lott and Actimage, and 30 years of digital entrepreneurship by Juergen Lukas, from the first mobile phone applications in the late 1990s to artificial intelligence today.

ParkstoryWhere industrial engineering meets digital intelligence.

These three histories share a common belief: that technology should challenge conventions, solve real problems, and continuously evolve. Parkstory is not a parking manufacturer that has added software to its machines. Mechanical architecture and software intelligence are developed as one integrated system from the outset.

The founders

Never simply another parking system.

Steffen Nussbaum, Juergen Lukas and Marc Lott founded Parkstory with a shared ambition: to fundamentally rethink automated parking and its role in modern infrastructure.

The objective was to overcome the limitations of conventional parking technology by developing an entirely different approach to how vehicles are stored, moved and managed.

Basement under a residential building
